results.summary_before: The Wave Generator produces sine, sawtooth, triangular, and square waveforms with selectable amplitude and phase parameters, outputting 8-bit two's complement fixed-point values in parallel or via a write-only SPI interface. It is configured by setting waveform selection pins and loading amplitude and phase values through a parameter bus, then enabling generation. An external SPI DAC is needed to convert the digital output to an analog signal. The design is notable for its flexible parameter control and the SPI interface that enables connection to a DAC, with a maximum sampling frequency of 1.65 MHz.
results.summary: The Wave Generator produces sine, sawtooth, triangular, and square waveforms with selectable amplitude and phase parameters, outputting 8-bit two's complement fixed-point values in parallel or via a write-only SPI interface. It is configured by setting waveform selection pins and loading amplitude and phase values through a parameter bus, then enabling generation. An external SPI DAC is needed to convert the digital output to an analog signal. The design provides flexible parameter control and SPI output for connecting to a DAC, with a maximum sampling frequency of 1.65 MHz.

results.summary_before: This is an analog voltage-controlled ring oscillator (VCRO) that uses transmission gates as delay control elements, based on a published paper. It provides an analog output and requires external control voltages on two pins, with the sum ideally equal to the 1.8V supply. The design is intended for testing and characterization of the oscillator's frequency tuning range. It is a transistor-level analog circuit with no digital interface.

results.summary_before: This design is an SPI-controlled PWM generator and 8-bit IO controller with two SPI interfaces for testing. It contains eight registers that configure PWM on-time and cycle, and eight IO pins that can be set as inputs or outputs. Testing involves reading an ID register and writing/reading back registers via SPI. External hardware needed is an SPI master device.

results.summary_before: This design uses a chain of flip-flops to display the word 'HELP' on a 7-segment display, with each flip-flop representing one letter and the last one blanking all segments. It has only seven outputs for the segments and no inputs, so it simply shows the sequence after reset. The project is a minimal demonstration and has been tested on silicon, with the author confirming that it displayed 'HELP'. No external hardware is required beyond the 7-segment display.
